back.body: INJURY IS ENERGY TRANSFERRED INTO TISSUE · SPEED MATTERS FAR MORE THAN WEIGHT — double the speed, roughly four times the energy · BLUNT: energy spread wide → serious INTERNAL injury with LITTLE TO SEE · PENETRATING: energy along a PATH → ask what is on the line between entry and where it stopped · THE SIZE OF THE HOLE TELLS YOU NOTHING · THREE COLLISIONS: vehicle into object → occupant into vehicle → ORGANS INTO THE INSIDE OF THE BODY · LOOK AT THE VEHICLE BEFORE IT IS TOWED: starred windscreen, bent wheel, intruded door · Mechanism raises suspicion — it NEVER replaces assessment
back.why_it_matters: Something bent that steering wheel and starred that windscreen, and that something was him.

front.title: Index of suspicion
front.summary: What you expect before you find anything

back.body: RAISED BY: ejection · DEATH OF ANOTHER OCCUPANT · falls · rollover · compartment intrusion · pedestrian or motorcyclist struck · NUMERIC THRESHOLDS COME FROM YOUR LOCAL TRAUMA TRIAGE CRITERIA — they vary and get revised, so use yours · OLDER PATIENTS ARE INJURED BY FAR LESS ENERGY — A FALL FROM STANDING IS A REAL MECHANISM AT 82 · CHILDREN compensate beautifully and then crash · ANTICOAGULANTS: same mechanism, much more bleeding · IT CHANGES: how hard you assess · how early you decide to go · what you say at handover · 'I FEEL FINE' DOES NOT LOWER IT
back.why_it_matters: A metre off the bottom step does not sound like a mechanism. At 82, on a blood thinner, it is one.

back.body: FOUR TIERS, IN ORDER · 1 PHYSIOLOGICAL: abnormal vitals or reduced consciousness NOW — outranks every theory · 2 ANATOMICAL: penetrating head/neck/torso, 2+ long bones, flail chest, pelvic fracture, amputation, paralysis · 3 MECHANISM: well-looking patient, enormous energy · 4 SPECIAL: age either end, ANTICOAGULATED, pregnant, burns — THE TIER MOST OFTEN SKIPPED · UNDER-TRIAGE IS FAR WORSE THAN OVER-TRIAGE, so the criteria are deliberately cautious — hesitating? Go to the trauma centre · TIME TO DEFINITIVE CARE beats geographical nearest · THE NUMBERS ARE YOUR LOCAL PROTOCOL'S, NOT A REMEMBERED ONE
back.why_it_matters: Under-triage costs an hour of transfer. Over-triage cost them fourteen minutes of driving.

back.body: See the algorithm card. Physiological → anatomical → mechanism → special considerations. A yes at any tier means trauma centre per local criteria, with a pre-alert. Only a no at all four goes to the closest appropriate facility.
back.why_it_matters: The fourth box is the one people never reach, because they stop looking after the third.

front.title: Golden period, platinum ten
front.summary: Do only what cannot be done moving

back.body: DEFINITIVE CARE = A SURGEON AND BLOOD — neither is on your ambulance · Every scene minute is a minute the treatment is not happening · The 'golden HOUR' is a TEACHING IDEA, not a biological deadline — time matters continuously, no cliff edge · PLATINUM TEN MINUTES = target scene time in major trauma · ON SCENE ONLY: failing AIRWAY · CATASTROPHIC BLEEDING · EXTRICATION · EN ROUTE: vitals, splinting, bandaging, secondary survey, history · LOAD AND GO IS GOOD CARE when the problem is inside the abdomen · Long scene times = SEQUENTIAL work, not slow movement — work in PARALLEL, do not rush
back.why_it_matters: Nobody rushed and nobody made a mistake. The eleven minutes were the mistake.

front.title: External bleeding control
front.summary: Press hard, one spot, and do not look

back.body: ARTERIAL = bright red, SPURTS with the pulse · VENOUS = darker, steady flow · CAPILLARY = oozes · CATASTROPHIC BLEEDING COMES BEFORE THE AIRWAY — it kills faster · DIRECT PRESSURE works when it is FIRM · FOCUSED ON ONE POINT · and HELD · Two fingertips on the bleeding point beat a palm on a wad of gauze · DO NOT LIFT THE DRESSING TO LOOK — every look tears apart what was forming · SOAKED THROUGH? ADD ON TOP and press harder — never remove · LIMB, pressure failing → TOURNIQUET, no hesitation · JUNCTIONAL (groin, armpit, neck) → PACK IT · ELEVATION AND PRESSURE POINTS ARE NO LONGER PRIMARY MEASURES
back.why_it_matters: It had not stopped. It had been starting to stop, twelve separate times.

front.title: Tourniquets
front.summary: Too loose is worse than none

back.body: FOR: life-threatening LIMB bleeding pressure has not controlled · pressure impractical · AMPUTATION · PROPERLY APPLIED TOURNIQUETS ARE SAFE — patients die from LATE ones, they rarely lose limbs to prompt ones · HIGH AND TIGHT above the wound · over a SINGLE BONE · NEVER OVER A JOINT · TIGHTEN UNTIL BLEEDING STOPS *AND* THE DISTAL PULSE IS GONE — both · TOO LOOSE BLOCKS VEINS BUT NOT ARTERIES AND MAKES BLEEDING WORSE — bleeding increased? TIGHTEN, do not remove · One not enough? SECOND ABOVE THE FIRST · IT WILL HURT — that is not a reason to loosen · NEVER COVER IT · WRITE THE TIME · NO FIELD RELEASE
back.why_it_matters: Everything about that tourniquet was right except that nobody could see it.

back.body: See the skill card steps. Critical: recognise the indication, HIGH AND TIGHT over a single bone, NEVER over a joint, tighten until BLEEDING STOPS AND DISTAL PULSE GONE, tighten further if bleeding increases, second tourniquet above the first if needed, WRITE THE TIME, NEVER COVER IT, do not loosen for pain, NO FIELD RELEASE, say 'tourniquet applied at [time]' out loud at handover.
back.why_it_matters: The two failures are applying it too loosely, and hiding it under a blanket.

front.title: Wound packing
front.summary: Tight, onto the source, and commit

back.body: FOR JUNCTIONAL WOUNDS a tourniquet cannot reach: GROIN · ARMPIT · NECK · deep torso-boundary wounds · NOT THE CHEST, NOT THE ABDOMEN — a cavity has no floor to pack against · FINGER IN, FIND THE BLEEDING POINT, PACK DIRECTLY ONTO IT · KEEP FEEDING GAUZE IN — far more than you expect · FILL THE WHOLE CAVITY TIGHTLY — loose packing is FAILED packing, just wet gauze · HEMOSTATIC GAUZE PACKS THE SAME WAY — the agent shortens the time, it does not pack itself · HOLD for the specified time WITHOUT LETTING GO · Secure with a pressure dressing · DO NOT REMOVE TO LOOK · GET HANDS TO HOLD THEM FIRST — this hurts more than almost anything
back.why_it_matters: It hurt twice, because the first time was gentle.

back.body: See the skill card steps. Critical: confirm the site (junctional, NOT chest or abdomen), get help to hold them BEFORE starting, finger in to find the source, pack DIRECTLY ONTO the bleeding point, keep feeding gauze, fill the cavity TIGHTLY, fist and body weight pressure, HOLD the full time without looking, secure with a pressure dressing, do NOT remove to inspect.
back.why_it_matters: Half-packing a wound means doing it twice, and twice hurts more than committing once.

back.body: CANNOT BE SEEN · CANNOT BE MEASURED · CANNOT BE FIXED BY YOU · WHERE IT HIDES: the floor, the CHEST, the ABDOMEN, the PELVIS, the THIGHS — litres, with nothing visible · RECOGNISE FROM MECHANISM: blunt abdominal, fall from height, crash with intrusion, penetrating torso, rib or pelvic fractures · AND FROM SHOCK, IN ORDER: RISING PULSE first → pale cool clammy → anxious → confused → quiet → THIRST → PRESSURE FALLS LAST · A NORMAL PRESSURE MEANS COMPENSATION, NOT SAFETY · BRUISING TAKES HOURS — its absence means nothing now · CARE: oxygen · KEEP WARM · position · nothing by mouth · GO TO A SURGEON
back.why_it_matters: The pulse and the hands were the only honest findings in the room.

back.body: SHOCK = INADEQUATE PERFUSION — low pressure is ONE LATE SIGN, not the definition · COMPENSATED: fast pulse · pale cool clammy · anxious · PRESSURE STILL NORMAL because the body is working flat out — THIS IS THE TRAP AND THE MOMENT TO ACT · DECOMPENSATED: pressure falls, mental status drops — LATE AND OMINOUS · CHILDREN HOLD THEIR PRESSURE AND THEN CRASH — a normal BP in an injured child is not reassurance · THE THREE THINGS YOU CAN DO: STOP EXTERNAL BLEEDING · KEEP THEM WARM · GET THEM TO A SURGEON · COLD BLOOD DOES NOT CLOT — blankets are a clotting intervention · SUPINE unless breathing prevents it; head-down is NOT routine · Nothing by mouth however thirsty
back.why_it_matters: Children hold their pressure until they cannot. The number tells you last.

front.title: Compensated vs decompensated
front.summary: The pressure is the last thing to change

back.body: See the comparison rows. Everything except the blood pressure has already changed by the time compensated shock is established — pulse, skin, capillary refill, mental status. Act in the left column.
back.why_it_matters: Compensated shock is a patient sprinting to stand still, and they cannot keep it up.

back.body: Most bleeds come from the FRONT of the septum and are fixable on a sofa · SIT UP AND LEAN FORWARD — NEVER TILT BACK, which sends blood into the stomach and brings it back as vomit · PINCH THE SOFT PART, NOT THE BONY BRIDGE · HOLD TEN MINUTES WITHOUT CHECKING · DO NOT PACK · ASK ABOUT ANTICOAGULANTS — heavier, longer, more often needs hospital · POSTERIOR BLEED: correct technique, little from the front, but they keep SWALLOWING → hospital · AFTER HEAD TRAUMA WITH CLEAR FLUID: DO NOT PACK, DO NOT PINCH — possible skull base fracture; let it drain · A nosebleed CAN cause shock in an older anticoagulated patient
back.why_it_matters: It had been going into her stomach for half an hour, and her stomach finally had enough of it.
